name: TCS New York City Marathon
headline: A 28-minute PR, built on a bold first half
summary: Your fastest marathon by far: 3:24:43, 28:26 quicker than Chicago and inside the top 10% of 61,051 finishers.
You went for sub-3:15 (7:26/mi) and ran miles 2–14 at 6:45–7:15, about 30 seconds a mile under goal pace. The half came in at 1:31:44, on track for roughly 3:03.

Miles 15–19, including the Queensboro Bridge, held at 7:33–7:48. The fade started at mile 20 (8:18), deepened through 21–23 (8:56–9:17), and peaked at 10:08 and 11:55 for miles 24–25 up Fifth Avenue and into the park, before a 9:01 mile 26.
Second half 1:52:59, a 21:15 positive split. The fitness for sub-3:15 was there through 19 miles; the early pace likely cost you the last 10K.
miles_source: Official NYRR mile splits (mile 13 interpolated from the half mark); miles 1–3 from your Garmin, scaled to the official 3-mile time

name: Chicago Marathon
headline: Locked in for 25K, then the wall
summary: After an 8:24 first 5K you settled into a remarkably even groove: 7:55–7:58 per mile for every 5K from 10K to 25K, on pace for about 3:28.
It slipped to 8:29 by 30K, 9:23 to 35K, then 11:36–11:57 over the last 7K: the classic wall after mile 19.
Half in 1:46:08, second half 2:07:01, a 20:53 positive split.
miles_source: Your watch: Strava GPS track, scaled to the 26.2-mile course

name: Marine Corps Marathon
headline: Patient, even, and the only negative split
summary: 4:08:17 at 9:29 per mile, finishing 5,304th of 16,167, inside the top third.
The most even race of the three: every 5K landed between 9:07 and 9:59 per mile, and you got faster at the end with a 9:07 stretch to 40K and an 8:35 close.
Half in 2:05:59, second half 2:02:18, a 3:41 negative split, the only one of your three marathons.
It came off a light build: 14 logged weeks averaging 21.6 miles, with a 20.1-mile long run.
miles_source: Your watch: Strava GPS track, scaled to the 26.2-mile course
